meta.source_system: 2048 merge mechanics (original open-source implementation gabrielecirulli/2048, MIT), transcribed as a deterministic 2x2 variant: slide + merge only, random tile spawns not collected
meta.source_citation: gabrielecirulli/2048, js/game_manager.js on master (fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/gabrielecirulli/2048): move() L130-191, getVector() L193-204, buildTraversals() L206-220, findFarthestPosition() L222-236, movesAvailable() L238-268, addRandomTile() L68-76; rules corroborated by Wikipedia '2048 (video game)', Gameplay section. Per-rule citations in meta.rules_with_citations; per-edge generating rules in meta.edge_rule_tags.
meta.state_encoding: state = 8 bits = 4 cells x 2 bits; cell c = 2*y + x with (x, y) = (column, row) in the source's convention -> cells 0=top-left, 1=top-right, 2=bottom-left, 3=bottom-right; per-cell encoding 0=empty, 1=value 2, 2=value 4, 3=unused (states containing a 3 in any cell = 175 padding states, every action self-loops reward 0); 81 real states
meta.semantics_class: direction-key: the four actions are the arrow keys bound to board coordinates (the original's own numbering 0:up, 1:right, 2:down, 3:left, game_manager.js L131). A board symmetry renames the keys with the cells, so true symmetries here are explicit-caliber claims; the fixed reading (keys pinned) is the naive contrast
meta.reward_rule: the 2048 score: +4 for a 2+2 -> 4 merge (game_manager.js L167 score += merged.value; the only merge allowed under the case's value cap), 0 for every other edge

rules_with_citations.rule: a move slides every tile as far as possible toward the chosen edge, stopped by another tile or the grid edge
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L152,172,222-236 (findFarthestPosition; moveTile to positions.farthest); Wikipedia "2048 (video game)", Gameplay: 'Tiles slide as far as possible in the chosen direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid.'

rules_with_citations.rule: two tiles of the same value that collide merge into one tile of the total value
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L156 (next.value === tile.value); 157 (tile.value * 2); Wikipedia "2048 (video game)", Gameplay: 'If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided.'

rules_with_citations.rule: a tile created by a merge cannot merge again within the same move
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L155 ('Only one merger per row traversal?'); 156 (!next.mergedFrom); 113-120 (prepareTiles clears mergedFrom at move start); Wikipedia "2048 (video game)", Gameplay: 'The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.' (On a 2-cell line this guard is automatically satisfied; cited because the transcribed rule is the original's.)

rules_with_citations.rule: the score increases by the value of the merged tile
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L167 (self.score += merged.value); Wikipedia "2048 (video game)", Gameplay: 'The user's score starts at zero, and is increased whenever two tiles combine, by the value of the new tile.'

rules_with_citations.rule: a move that slides nothing and merges nothing leaves the board and the score unchanged
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L175-177 (moved stays false when no tile moved); 182-190 (if (moved) {...} -- nothing happens otherwise); transcribed as a deterministic self-loop with reward 0

rules_with_citations.rule: the four actions are the arrow keys, numbered 0: up, 1: right, 2: down, 3: left
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L131 ('0: up, 1: right, 2: down, 3: left'); 194-204 (getVector map)

rules_with_citations.rule: NOT COLLECTED: after a moved move the original spawns a random tile (value 2 with probability 0.9, else 4) in a random empty cell
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L182-183 (if (moved) { this.addRandomTile(); ... }); 68-76 (addRandomTile: Math.random() < 0.9 ? 2 : 4); Wikipedia "2048 (video game)", Gameplay: 'another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn.' -- randomness is outside the deterministic FSM semantics; recorded, not repaired

rules_with_citations.rule: a board where no direction changes anything self-loops on every action (no legal move changes the deterministic state)
rules_with_citations.citation: gabrielecirulli/2048 js/game_manager.js (MIT) L184-187 (movesAvailable() false -> over=true); 238-268 (movesAvailable/tileMatchesAvailable); Wikipedia "2048 (video game)", Gameplay: 'When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.' -- in the no-spawn variant deadness reduces to: no direction changes the board

rules_with_citations.rule: VARIANT BOUNDARY: merging is capped at 4 -- only 2+2 merges (into 4); two 4s slide without merging
rules_with_citations.citation: the original has no cap (game_manager.js L156-157 merge any equal pair, L170 only watches for 2048); the cap is this case's deliberate 2x2 truncation, recorded in meta.transcription_notes

edge_rule_tags.layout: edge_rule_tags.values[s] is a 4-character string, character a in {M,S,N,P} = the generating rule of edge (s, action a); M=merged (R2/R3/R4), S=slid without merging (R1), N=no-op self-loop (R5), P=padding self-loop

meta.known_issue: engine explicit-caliber limitation discovered by this case (2026-11-03, crew-chief ruling: record as observed, fix upstream next wave): the vendored judge's explicit layer applies ONE declared action_map to every closed group element including the identity, so on any model with behaviorally distinguishable actions the identity element forces the identity map and no non-trivial renamed-action symmetry can be admitted. g1/g3/g4 are true symmetries under per-element action maps (derivation asserted by the generator; table in meta.per_element_action_maps); their explicit-caliber rejects are expected to flip after the upstream fix. Diagnosis: cases/mini2048/README.md; live receipts: cases/mini2048/receipts/.
transcription_notes: scope: 2x2 board, cell values {empty, 2, 4}; the deterministic core of 2048 (slide + merge) with the random tile spawn NOT collected (rule R7) -- randomness is not part of the deterministic FSM semantics, per the court's not-collected discipline (same pattern as the tcp case's any-state RST edges).

VARIANT BOUNDARY (rule R9): the merge is capped at 4 (2+2 -> 4 only; two 4s never merge here). The original merges any equal pair (game_manager.js L156-157). Without the cap a 2x2 board still has a finite reachable set, but the 8/16/... value ladder would need wider cell encodings; the cap keeps the transcription inside 2 bits per cell and is applied identically in all four directions, so the board symmetry group is preserved.
actions: indexed with the original's own numbering 0:up, 1:right, 2:down, 3:left (game_manager.js L131) -- action indices are source data, not a court choice.

encoding: state = 8 bits = 4 cells x 2 bits; per-cell encoding 0=empty, 1=value 2, 2=value 4, 3=unused. The 175 states containing a cell with encoding 3 are unreachable padding: every action self-loops with reward 0 (same padding convention as tcp/dhcp/imap states 11..15). Moves never create encoding 3, so real states (81 of them) only reach real states.

dead boards: a board that no direction changes self-loops on all four actions with reward 0 (rule R5/R8) -- this is the original's own behavior for a move that changes nothing, not a padding convention.

rewards: the 2048 score (rule R4): +4 for the only allowed merge (2+2 -> 4), 0 otherwise. Unlike tcp/dhcp/imap (all-zero rewards) the reward layer here carries the game's payoff; the explicit/fixed contrast therefore also has a reward-profile reading.

reward variant boundary (audit 2026-11-03): a move containing two 2+2 merges (state [2,2;2,2]) awards +4 flat; the original L167 per-merge sum would be +8. Transitions identical; no verdict depends on this.

explicit caliber note: a board symmetry renames the direction keys element-by-element (rotating the board clockwise turns 'up' into 'right'); rho(identity)=id while rho(rot90)!=id, so no single action_map can serve a whole closed group. The engine's group format carries ONE semantics.action_map; each explicit group file here declares the map of its named generator, and meta.per_element_action_maps holds the full derivation (computed and asserted by this generator on every run).
